mainTopic: How the מצוה of פריה ורביה is fulfilled: משה's example, רבי נתן's reports of בית שמאי and בית הלל, a convert's earlier children, and children who died.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a back-and-forth about the מצוה of פריה ורביה. Why don't בית הלל learn from משה, who separated from his wife after two sons? The answer is that משה acted on his own reasoning. A ברייתא lists three things משה decided on his own, and ה׳ agreed with each one: separating from his wife, breaking the לוחות, and adding a day before מתן תורה. The גמרא then brings two ברייתות in which רבי נתן reports the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל differently, along with the פסוקים behind each version. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether a convert's children from before he converted count. They are consistent with how they rule about a בכור for inheritance. This leads to a discussion of whether gentiles and slaves have family lineage. Finally, רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue whether a man whose children died has fulfilled the מצוה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a challenge to רב הונא from a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the rejection: we can't learn from what was impossible
steps.stepSummary: These two words finish בית שמאי's rejection of בית הלל's proof from creation. ה׳ created one male and one female only because there was no other way, so it proves nothing about the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We do not learn what is possible] from what was not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from just before. ה׳ making only one man and one woman cannot teach us the rule, because at creation it was the only way to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל wanted to prove from creation ('male and female He created them') that you need a son and a daughter. בית שמאי answer that creation had no choice: one couple was the only possible way to start the world. A rule for normal people, who can have any mix of children, can't be learned from a case with no options.

keyTerms.meaning: not possible, there was no other way

phrases.english: from what is not possible.
phrases.notes: We don't learn a normal case from creation, where one couple was the only option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the previous challenge: why בית שמאי do not learn from creation. You cannot learn a possible case from one where there was no other option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the creation of one male and one female as a source for the מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Creation was a forced, no-choice case, and you can't learn a rule for normal cases from it.

steps.title: Why don't בית הלל learn from משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: משה stopped after two sons, so why not learn from him that two sons is enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל too, let them learn from משה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to בית הלל and asks why they ignore the example of משה, who separated from his wife after having two sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי learned their view (two sons is enough) from משה, who had גרשום and אליעזר and then separated from his wife. If that is a real source, בית הלל should have to accept it too. The challenge pushes בית הלל to explain why משה's behavior isn't a proof.

phrases.english: And בית הלל too,
let them learn from משה!
phrases.notes: משה separated from his wife after two sons, so two sons should be enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending בית שמאי, the גמרא now challenges בית הלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that two sons do not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה stopped having children after two sons, which seems to show that two sons is enough.

steps.title: משה acted on his own reasoning
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that משה separated from his wife because of his own reasoning, not because the מצוה was finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: They will tell you: משה did it on his own understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for בית הלל. משה's separation was his own personal decision for a special reason, so it is no rule for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes what משה's action proves. He did not stop because he had finished פריה ורביה. He stopped because of his unique closeness to ה׳. So it tells us nothing about how many children an ordinary person needs.

keyTerms.meaning: on his own understanding, by his own decision

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean משה did something wrong. The next step shows that ה׳ agreed with him. It only means his reason was special to him, not a general rule about פריה ורביה.

phrases.english: They will tell you:
משה did it on his own understanding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ: מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתֵּיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against בית הלל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: משה's action came from a special personal reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה stopped because two sons finish the מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה stopped because of his own reasoning tied to his role as prophet, so no general rule comes from it.

steps.title: The ברייתא: three things משה did on his own
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer. משה did three things on his own and ה׳ agreed with him: he separated from his wife, broke the לוחות, and added a day before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: משה did three things on his own understanding, and his understanding matched ה׳'s: he separated from his wife, he broke the לוחות, and he added one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that separating from his wife was משה's own decision. The ברייתא lists it among three such decisions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that separating from his wife was something משה decided 'מדעתו', on his own. That backs up בית הלל's answer. It also says ה׳ agreed each time, which sets up the next steps that explain each decision.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: As it was taught: משה did three things on his own understanding,
and his understanding agreed with ה׳'s understanding:
he separated from his wife,
and he broke the Tablets,
and he added one day.
phrases.notes: This is the extra day of getting ready before ה׳ gave the תורה at הר סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה מִדַּעְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a ברייתא supporting the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That משה's separation from his wife was his own decision.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing three things משה did on his own that ה׳ agreed with.

steps.title: What reasoning led משה to separate from his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning משה used when he decided to separate from his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He separated from his wife: what did he learn [that led him to this]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the ברייתא. It asks how משה reached his decision to separate from his wife, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said משה acted on his own understanding, but it did not say how he reasoned. This question asks for the logic behind his decision.

keyTerms.meaning: what did he learn or reason out?

phrases.english: He separated from his wife:
what did he reason out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first item in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning משה used to separate from his wife.

steps.title: משה's קל וחומר from the people at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned: if the people, whom ה׳ spoke to only once at a set time, had to stay away from their wives, then I, whom ה׳ may speak to at any moment, surely must.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The Jewish people, to whom the שכינה spoke only for a short time and at a set time, were told by the תורה 'Do not approach a woman.' I, who am set aside for ה׳'s speech at every moment and have no set time, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives משה's reasoning, which is a קל וחומר (a 'how much more so' argument). If the lighter case needs separation, the stronger case surely does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people only had to separate for a few days before one set meeting with the שכינה. משה could be spoken to at any moment with no warning, so he always had to be ready. That is why he separated for good. The reason has nothing to do with how many children he had.

keyTerms.meaning: reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: He said: If the Jewish people,
with whom the שכינה spoke
only for a limited time,
and He set a time for them,
the Torah said: 'Do not approach a woman'
phrases.notes: שמות 19:15

phrases.english: then I, who am set aside for [ה׳'s] speech
at every single moment,
and He did not set a time for me,
all the more so [must I separate].

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: וּמָה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁלֹּא דִּבְּרָה עִמָּהֶם שְׁכִינָה אֶלָּא לְפִי שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the people at Sinai to משה, who had to be ready for prophecy at all times.

steps.title: ה׳ agreed: 'You, stand here with Me'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows ה׳ agreed. The people were told to go back to their tents, but משה was told to stay with ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his understanding agreed with ה׳'s, as it says: 'Go tell them: Return to your tents. And you, stand here with Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק that ה׳ approved of משה's separating from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Return to your tents' let the people go back home to their wives after מתן תורה. משה was told 'stand here with Me', so he stayed separate. This confirms that ה׳ agreed with his decision.

keyTerms.meaning: return to your tents (go back to family life)

steps.whatToRemember: משה separated from his wife because of his constant prophecy, not because he had finished פריה ורביה. So בית הלל are not forced to learn from him that two sons is enough.

phrases.english: And his understanding agreed with ה׳'s understanding,
as it is said: 'Go say to them,
phrases.notes: דברים 5:26–27

phrases.english: Return to your tents.
And you, stand here with Me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves ה׳'s approval of the reasoning in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ agreed with משה separating from his wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 5:26–27, 'Return to your tents... and you, stand here with Me.'

steps.title: What reasoning led משה to break the לוחות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second item in the ברייתא and asks why משה broke the לוחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He broke the לוחות: what did he reason out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second thing משה did on his own. It asks for his reasoning, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as step 5, now about breaking the לוחות after עגל הזהב.

phrases.english: He broke the Tablets:
what did he reason out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first item of the ברייתא to the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning משה used to break the לוחות.

steps.title: משה's קל וחומר from the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned: if a Jew who has turned away may not eat the פסח, which is just one מצוה, then a nation serving an idol surely may not receive the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The פסח is one of the 613 מצוות, and the תורה said 'No outsider may eat of it.' The whole תורה, when the Jewish people have turned to idol worship, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives משה's reasoning, again a קל וחומר. This time he compares the קרבן פסח to the whole Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'outsider' (בן נכר) includes a Jew who has turned away from ה׳, and he is barred from just one מצוה, the פסח. The לוחות stood for the entire תורה, and the people were worshipping עגל הזהב. So משה concluded they were surely not fit to receive the לוחות.

keyTerms.meaning: an outsider, someone estranged from ה׳
Jews who have turned away from ה׳

phrases.english: He said: If the פסח,
which is one of six hundred
and thirteen מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה ״כׇּל בֶּן נֵכָר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״.
phrases.english: the Torah said: 'No outsider shall eat of it.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:43. This 'outsider' also includes a Jew who has turned away from ה׳.

phrases.english: [Here it is] the whole Torah, and the Jewish people have turned away,
all the more so [they may not receive it].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: וּמָה פֶּסַח, שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד מִשֵּׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the פסח, one מצוה barred to a Jew who turned away, to the whole Torah when the people served an idol.

steps.title: ה׳ agreed: 'Well done for breaking them'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר שברת' show ה׳ approved. ריש לקיש reads אשר as a hint to 'יישר כחך', meaning 'well done for breaking them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And his understanding agreed with ה׳'s, as it is written 'that you broke.' And ריש לקיש said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה, 'Well done that you broke them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves from a פסוק, as explained by ריש לקיש, that ה׳ approved of משה breaking the לוחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אשר' sounds like 'יישר', so ריש לקיש reads it as ה׳ saying 'יישר כחך', a phrase of praise. That turns a simple reference to the broken לוחות into ה׳'s approval of breaking them.

keyTerms.meaning: may your strength be firm, a phrase meaning 'well done'

steps.whatToRemember: Both separating from his wife and breaking the לוחות were משה's own decisions, each built on a קל וחומר, and ה׳ agreed with both, as פסוקים show.

phrases.english: And his understanding agreed with ה׳'s understanding,
as it is written: 'that you broke,'
phrases.notes: שמות 34:1

phrases.english: and ריש לקיש said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה:
Well done that you broke [them].
phrases.notes: He hears the word אשר as sounding like יישר, a word of praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִסְכִּימָה דַּעְתּוֹ לְדַעַת הַמָּקוֹם, דִּכְתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר שִׁבַּרְתָּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves ה׳'s approval of the reasoning in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ agreed with משה breaking the לוחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 34:1 'אשר שברת', as read by ריש לקיש: 'יישר כחך ששברת.'

steps.title: Why did משה add a day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third item in the ברייתא and asks what reasoning led משה to add a day of separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He added one day on his own. What did he learn from the text?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third thing משה did on his own and asks what he learned that made him add a day. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ told משה to prepare the people for two days. משה made it three. The גמרא wants to know which reading of the פסוק led him to do that.

keyTerms.meaning: On his own, from his own thinking
What did he learn from the text?

phrases.english: He added one day on his own,
what did he learn from the text?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹסִיף יוֹם אֶחָד מִדַּעְתּוֹ, מַאי דְּרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 8: after the לוחות, the גמרא moves to the third item in the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק led משה to add a day.

steps.title: Today is like tomorrow, so the night counts
steps.stepSummary: משה read 'today and tomorrow' as one rule: each day needs its night. Today's night had already passed, so he needed two full days after this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written, 'Make them holy today and tomorrow.' Today is like tomorrow. Tomorrow includes the night before it, so today must also include the night before it. Today's night had already passed, so we learn he needed two days besides today.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains משה's reasoning. The word 'today' is compared to 'tomorrow,' so each day of preparation must include its night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full day of preparation includes the night before it, the way 'tomorrow' clearly does. ה׳ spoke to משה in the morning, after that night was over, so the current day could not count as a full day. That left two full days still needed, so the total became three.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And make them holy today and tomorrow.'
phrases.notes: שמות 19:10

phrases.english: Today is like tomorrow:
just as tomorrow has its night with it,
phrases.notes: The night before a day counts together with that day.

phrases.english: so too today has its night with it.
And the night of today had already gone by,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי לְבַר מֵהָאִידָּנָא.
phrases.english: so learn from this: two days not counting today.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Today must be like tomorrow, a full day with its night. Since today's night was over, משה needed two more full days.

steps.title: ה׳ agreed: the שכינה came on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The proof that ה׳ agreed is that the שכינה did not rest on the mountain until שבת, the day משה had calculated.
steps.simpleTranslation: His thinking matched ה׳'s, since the שכינה did not rest on the mountain until שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves ה׳ approved of משה's extra day. מתן תורה happened on שבת, which fits משה's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ had meant only two days, the תורה would have been given a day earlier. Since the שכינה came only on שבת, the third day, it shows ה׳ agreed with משה. This matches the pattern of Steps 7 and 10, where each of משה's choices is backed up.
steps.whatToRemember: All three things משה did on his own were approved by ה׳: separating from his wife, breaking the לוחות, and adding a day.

phrases.english: And his thinking matched ה׳'s thinking —
since the שכינה did not rest on the mountain until שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of Step 12 by showing ה׳ agreed.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ approved משה's added day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The שכינה rested on הר סיני only on שבת.

steps.title: רבי נתן's first report: four children or two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי נתן reports that בית שמאי require two sons and two daughters for פרו ורבו, and בית הלל require a son and a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי נתן says, בית שמאי say two males and two females. בית הלל say a male and a female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of פרו ורבו and brings a ברייתא with a different report of the disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new version of the argument about how many children a person must have to fulfill פרו ורבו. According to רבי נתן, בית שמאי require four children: two of each. בית הלל require one of each.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
Beit Shammai say:
two males and two females,
and Beit Hillel say: a male and a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of משה and returns to the main topic of פרו ורבו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי נתן: בית שמאי require two sons and two daughters, and בית הלל require a son and a daughter.

steps.title: רב הונא asks for בית שמאי's source
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks what source supports בית שמאי's opinion of four children in רבי נתן's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is the reason of רבי נתן's version of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks where בית שמאי get the idea of four children. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four children is a big requirement, so we need a source. The question is only about this ברייתא's version of בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Natan
according to Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: He means the opinion רבי נתן reports in the name of בית שמאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נָתָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the בית שמאי opinion in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for requiring two sons and two daughters.

steps.title: אדם and חוה had four children
steps.stepSummary: The extra word את shows הבל and קין were each born with a sister. After הבל died, חוה was given שת to replace him, which shows four children were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And she again gave birth to his brother הבל.' This means הבל and his sister, and קין and his sister. And it is written: 'ה׳ has given me another child in place of הבל, since קין killed him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings two פסוקים. The first shows אדם and חוה had two sons and two daughters. The second shows that when one son was lost, ה׳ replaced him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'את' hints that a sister was born with each brother, so there were four children. When הבל was killed, ה׳ gave שת 'in place of הבל' to bring the number back to two sons and two daughters. This suggests four is the required number.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And she again gave birth to
his brother, Abel':
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:2. The extra word את is read as hinting that a sister was born too.

phrases.english: Abel and his sister, Cain and his sister,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״כִּי שָׁת לִי אֱלֹהִים זֶרַע אַחֵר
phrases.english: and it is written: 'For God has given me another child
in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:25

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַתּוֹסֶף לָלֶדֶת אֶת אָחִיו אֶת הָבֶל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אדם and חוה had two sons and two daughters, and a replacement was given for הבל, so four children are required.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן explain the פסוק about שת being 'in place of הבל.' These are the תנאים who disagree with רבי נתן and report בית שמאי as requiring two sons, not four children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who hold that בית שמאי require only two sons, deal with the פסוק about שת. This sets up a short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק shows that four children were needed and a lost one had to be replaced, why don't the רבנן accept רבי נתן's version, that בית שמאי require four? The question pushes them to explain the פסוק differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And the רבנן (here, the תנאים who disagree with רבי נתן's report of בית שמאי)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means the תנאים who say בית שמאי require two sons: how do they explain this פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other opinion deals with the proof of Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן, who report בית שמאי as requiring two sons, explain the פסוק of 'another child in place of הבל.'

steps.title: חוה was just thanking ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say חוה's words were only thanks to ה׳, not a sign that four children are required.
steps.simpleTranslation: She was just giving thanks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חוה was simply thanking ה׳ for a new child. Her words teach no rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the force out of רב הונא's proof. 'In place of הבל' is read as an expression of gratitude, not as ה׳ filling a required count. So the פסוק does not prove that four children are needed.

phrases.english: She was just giving thanks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by reading the פסוק as thanks.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חוה's words were thanks to ה׳, not a rule about how many children are needed.

steps.title: רבי נתן's second report: two children or one
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא reports רבי נתן differently: בית שמאי require a son and a daughter, and בית הלל say a son or a daughter is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: רבי נתן says, בית שמאי say a male and a female. בית הלל say either a male or a female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that reports רבי נתן's version of the argument in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each opinion asks for less than in the first ברייתא. בית שמאי now say one of each, and בית הלל say just one child of either kind is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא: Rabbi Natan says:
Beit Shammai say: a male and a female,
and Beit Hillel say:
either a male or a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different report of רבי נתן's version, in place of Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per this ברייתא: בית שמאי require a son and a daughter, and בית הלל say one child of either kind is enough.

steps.title: רבא asks for בית הלל's source
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what source supports בית הלל's opinion in this ברייתא, that one child is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רבי נתן's version of בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks why one child would be enough according to בית הלל. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as רב הונא's question in Step 15. This time the question is about the smaller requirement in the second ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Natan
according to Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי נָתָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the בית הלל opinion in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for one child being enough.

steps.title: The world was made to be lived in
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ה׳ made the world to be lived in. Anyone who has even one child has added to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in.' And this person has made it more lived in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a פסוק showing that the goal is to fill the world with people. Even one child adds to that goal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source here is the purpose of creation, not a set number. A person who has one child, of either kind, has added people to the world, so he has fulfilled the purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן's version of the argument is reported two ways. One says four children or two, from קין and הבל. The other says two children or one, from 'לשבת יצרה.'

phrases.english: As it says: 'He did not create it to be empty;
He formed it to be lived in,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:18

phrases.english: and this person has made it more lived in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world was made to be lived in, and one child already adds to that.

steps.title: Did a convert with children from before fulfill the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about whether a man who had children as a gentile and then converted has fulfilled פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a man had children while he was a gentile and then he converted, רבי יוחנן says he has fulfilled פריה ורביה, and ריש לקיש says he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a disagreement between two אמוראים about a convert's children from before he converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא asked how many children a person needs. Now it asks a new question: do children born before the father converted count at all? רבי יוחנן says they count and ריש לקיש says they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was stated." This opens a disagreement between אמוראים.

phrases.english: It was stated:
If he had children when he was a gentile
and then he converted,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
He has fulfilled the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply.
And Reish Lakish said:
He has not fulfilled the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic within the laws of פריה ורביה: whether children born before conversion count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: he has fulfilled פריה ורביה. ריש לקיש: he has not.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason is that the man already had children. ריש לקיש's reason is that a convert is like a newborn baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he fulfilled the מצוה because he already had children. ריש לקיש says he did not, because a person who converts is like a newly born child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion, this time adding the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the facts count: the children exist, so the מצוה is done. For ריש לקיש, conversion is a fresh start, so everything from his old life, including his children, no longer counts legally.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert is like a newborn child: a complete new start

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that a convert is like a newborn is a famous principle that shows up in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said he has fulfilled the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply
because he already had them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the children he had before converting.

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לֹא קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said he has not fulfilled the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply
because a convert who has converted
is like a child who was just born.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה — דְּהָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the two opinions from step 22 and adds the reasoning for each.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the children exist, so the מצוה is done. ריש לקיש: a convert is like a newborn, so earlier children do not count.

steps.title: The same dispute about a firstborn's inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש keep the same reasoning in a second dispute: whether the first son born after the conversion is a בכור for inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, because it was also stated: if a man had children as a gentile and then converted, רבי יוחנן says he has no בכור for inheritance, since he already had "the first of his strength." ריש לקיש says he does have a בכור for inheritance, because a convert is like a newborn child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the same two אמוראים argue the same way in another area of law, inheritance by a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור gets a double share, and the Torah calls him "the first of his strength": the father's first child. רבי יוחנן says the father's first child was already born before the conversion, so a son born afterward is not a בכור. ריש לקיש says the conversion was a fresh start, so the first son born afterward is a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning (they are being consistent)
A firstborn for inheritance, who receives a double share
"The first of his strength." The Torah's description of a firstborn.

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the flip. In this case רבי יוחנן says "no" and ריש לקיש says "yes," but each one has the same reasoning as before. רבי יוחנן counts the earlier children, and ריש לקיש does not.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated:
If he had children when he was a gentile and then he converted,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
He has no firstborn for inheritance,
because he already had "the first of his strength."
phrases.notes: דברים 21:17

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
He does have a firstborn for inheritance,
because a convert who has converted is like a child who was just born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that both אמוראים are consistent by quoting a parallel dispute about inheritance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no בכור for inheritance after conversion. ריש לקיש: there is a בכור for inheritance after conversion.

steps.title: Why the inheritance dispute had to be stated too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that from the פריה ורביה case alone, we might have thought רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש about inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the first case, I would say רבי יוחנן holds his view there because gentiles are commanded in פריה ורביה even before converting. But about inheritance, since gentiles are not part of those laws, I might think he agrees with ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a "צריכא" explanation, showing why we need both disputes. This step covers the first half: why the inheritance case is necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentiles are also commanded to have children, so it makes sense that children born before conversion still count toward that מצוה. Inheritance is different, because gentiles are not part of those laws. So we might have guessed that רבי יוחנן would treat inheritance as a fresh start. The second dispute teaches us that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it is necessary." This explains why two similar statements are both needed.

phrases.english: And it is necessary to state both:
because if it had taught us only that first case,
I would say it is in that case that Rabbi Yochanan said his view
because from the start too
they are commanded to be fruitful and multiply,
phrases.notes: "They" means gentiles, even before converting.

phrases.english: but regarding inheritance,
since they are not part of the laws of inheritance,
I might say he agrees with Reish Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why both disputes are recorded, starting with why the inheritance case is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The unspoken question: why do we need both disputes, if the reasoning is the same?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the פריה ורביה case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן's view applies only there, because gentiles are already commanded in that מצוה.

steps.title: Why the first dispute was needed, and both are necessary
steps.stepSummary: From the inheritance case alone, we might have thought ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן about פריה ורביה. So both disputes are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had been stated only about inheritance, I would say ריש לקיש holds his view there. But in the פריה ורביה case, I might think he agrees with רבי יוחנן. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by giving the other side, then concludes that both disputes needed to be recorded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's "fresh start" view fits inheritance well, since gentiles are not part of those laws anyway. But for פריה ורביה, which gentiles are already commanded in, we might have thought even ריש לקיש counts the earlier children. The first dispute shows that he holds the "fresh start" view there too.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is necessary." Both statements had to be said.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says children born before conversion count, both for פריה ורביה and for blocking a later בכור. ריש לקיש says a convert is like a newborn, so they count for neither. Each case teaches something we could not learn from the other.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only about this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is inheritance, the one just mentioned.

phrases.english: I would say it is in this case that Reish Lakish said his view,
but in that case,
phrases.notes: "That case" is the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply.

phrases.english: I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan,
so it is necessary to state both.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא — בְּהָא קָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכא and concludes it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both disputes are needed. Without each one, we might have thought one אמורא agrees with the other in that case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a verse about a gentile king
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a פסוק that calls a gentile king 'son of' his father, to show that gentiles have real family lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from the פסוק: 'At that time בראדך בלאדן, son of בלאדן, king of Babylon, sent...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view that a convert is like a newborn baby. He uses a פסוק that treats a gentile as the real son of his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנ"ך calls the gentile king 'son of בלאדן', so gentiles have family lineage. If so, a gentile's children should count as his, and after he converts he should already have fulfilled פריה ורביה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
Son of; here it suggests a real family connection

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
"At that time sent
Berodach-baladan, son of Baladan,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 20:12. The point is the words 'son of': a gentile is called his father's son.

phrases.english: king of Babylon, etc."!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the core dispute in steps 22-23 and challenges ריש לקיש directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a convert is like a newborn and his earlier children do not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק gives gentiles family lineage ('son of'), so a gentile's children are legally his children.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers that conversion cuts off lineage
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש agrees gentiles have lineage, but says that once they convert, that lineage is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: while they are gentiles, they have lineage. Once they convert, they have no lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש accepts what the פסוק shows but limits it. It applies only while the person is still a gentile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק proves gentiles have family lineage. It does not prove the lineage survives גירות. Conversion makes a fresh start, so the earlier children no longer count as his.

keyTerms.meaning: Family lineage, a legal family connection

phrases.english: He said to him:
While they are gentiles, they have lineage;
once they convert, they have no lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to the time before conversion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gentiles have lineage, so a convert's earlier children count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lineage exists only before conversion; גירות cuts it off.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, a gentile has lineage, but conversion erases it. That is why his earlier children do not count for him.

steps.title: רב: everyone agrees a slave has no lineage
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a slave has no family lineage, and learns it from the words 'with the donkey'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: everyone agrees that a slave has no lineage, as it is written, 'Stay here with the donkey,' meaning a nation that is like a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a related rule: no one argues that a slave has family lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם told his servants to stay 'with the donkey.' רב reads עִם (with) as עַם (nation), a people like a donkey. A donkey has no legal family line, and neither does a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: A nation that is like a donkey

phrases.english: Rav said:
Everyone agrees about a slave
that he has no lineage,
as it is written: "Stay here
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:5. אברהם is speaking to his servants.

phrases.english: with the donkey":
a nation that is like a donkey.
phrases.notes: רב reads the word 'with' (עִם) as if it said 'nation' (עַם).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from converts to a related case, slaves and lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave has no family lineage, and both sides agree on this.

steps.title: Challenge from ציבא, a slave who had sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a פסוק saying the slave ציבא had fifteen sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'And ציבא had fifteen sons and twenty slaves'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems to give a slave real sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציבא was a slave, yet the פסוק calls his children 'his sons.' That looks like family lineage for a slave, against רב.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And Ziba had fifteen sons
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 9:10.

phrases.english: and twenty slaves"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a slave has no lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls a slave's children 'his sons,' which suggests family lineage.

steps.title: 'Son' can just mean offspring, like 'a bull, son of cattle'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that 'son' here only means a biological child, as when an animal is called a 'son of cattle.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: it is like 'a bull, son of cattle.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that the word 'son' does not always mean legal lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says פַּר בֶּן בָּקָר, and animals have no legal family line. So 'son' can simply mean offspring. ציבא's 'sons' are his children by birth, not his legal family.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
It is like "a bull, son of cattle."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב כְּפַר בֶּן בָּקָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the word 'son' as plain offspring
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Sons' can mean offspring only, with no legal lineage.

steps.title: Then the gentile king's verse should be read the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why 'son of' in the בראדך בלאדן פסוק can't also mean just offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב אחא's answer back on the earlier proof. If 'son' can mean offspring, the פסוק about the gentile king proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 relied on 'son of בלאדן' to show gentiles have lineage. Step 31 just said 'son' can mean only offspring. So the step 27 proof seems to fall away.

phrases.english: If so,
here too!
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק about בראדך בלאדן from step 27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 31 to weaken the proof of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 27 that gentiles have lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'son' can mean just offspring, 'son of בלאדן' does not prove lineage either.

steps.title: The king's verse names both him and his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the king's פסוק names him and his father, which shows lineage, while ציבא's sons are never named.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it traced them by their own names and by their father's name. Here, it doesn't spell it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the two פסוקים are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a person and his father shows a real family line. The ציבא פסוק just counts 'fifteen sons' with no names, so it means only offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not spell it out

steps.confusionAlert: 'There' and 'here' have switched. In this step, 'there' is the gentile king and 'here' is ציבא, the opposite of step 32.

phrases.english: It is different there,
for it traced them by their names
and by their father's name,
but here it does not specify.
phrases.notes: ציבא's sons are counted but never named.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים use 'son' the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming the father shows lineage; an unnamed count of sons does not.

steps.title: Another answer: elsewhere gentiles are traced back two generations
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: another פסוק traces a gentile king to his father and grandfather, which clearly shows lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: in another place the פסוק traced them by their father and their father's father, as it is written: 'And King אסא sent them to בן הדד, son of טברימון, son of חזיון, king of ארם, who lived in Damascus, saying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer for why gentiles have lineage, using another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tracing a gentile back through father and grandfather is a real family line, not just 'offspring.' So gentile lineage is proven even apart from the בראדך פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Gentiles have family lineage, as the תנ"ך traces them through fathers and grandfathers. A slave has no lineage. According to ריש לקיש, a convert loses his lineage.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
it traced their lineage in another place
by their father and their father's father,
as it is written: "And King Asa sent them

phrases.aramaic: אֶל בֶּן הֲדַד בֶּן טַבְרִימּוֹן בֶּן חֶזְיוֹן
phrases.english: to Ben-hadad, son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 15:18

phrases.english: king of Aram, who dwelled in Damascus, saying."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 32, alongside step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only proof of gentile lineage is the בראדך פסוק, which could mean just offspring.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another פסוק traces gentiles through two generations, so they clearly have lineage.

steps.title: New dispute: a man whose children died
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן argue whether a man whose children died has fulfilled פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a man had children and they died, רב הונא said he fulfilled פריה ורביה. רבי יוחנן said he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new dispute between אמוראים. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the מצוה is done once children are born, or whether the children must still be alive. רב הונא says having them was enough. רבי יוחנן says it does not count if they died.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)

phrases.english: It was stated:
If he had children and they died,
Rav Huna said:
He has fulfilled being fruitful and multiplying.
Rabbi Yochanan said: He has not fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about fulfilling פריה ורביה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: a man whose children died has fulfilled פריה ורביה. רבי יוחנן: he has not.

steps.title: רב הונא's reason: bringing souls into the world
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds the man fulfilled the מצוה, based on רב אסי's teaching that בן דוד will not come until every soul waiting to be born has entered a body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said he fulfilled the מצוה, because of what רב אסי taught: בן דוד will not come until all the souls in the 'body' are used up, as the פסוק says, 'For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא says a man whose children died still fulfilled פריה ורביה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אסי, a goal of having children is to bring souls into bodies, so the world can reach the time of בן דוד. Once a child is born, a soul has entered a body and that goal is reached. The child dying later does not undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of David, meaning משיח
Literally 'body.' Here it is the place where unborn souls wait

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, for רב הונא, the מצוה is measured by the birth itself, not by how long the children live.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: he has fulfilled it
because of Rav Asi's teaching.
As Rav Asi said:
The son of David does not come
until all the souls in the 'body' are used up,
phrases.notes: All the souls waiting to be born must first enter bodies.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 57:16

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: קִיֵּים — מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רב הונא's position in the argument stated in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man whose children died has fulfilled פריה ורביה, because the birth already brought a soul into a body.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: the world must be inhabited
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the man did not fulfill the מצוה, because the purpose is that the world be inhabited (לשבת יצרה), and with his children dead that is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said he did not fulfill פריה ורביה, because we need 'He formed it to be inhabited,' and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן says the man has not fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן uses a different verse: the world was made to be lived in. A man fulfills the מצוה by leaving living people in the world. If his children died, he is not adding to the world's population, so the מצוה is not done.

keyTerms.meaning: He formed it (the world) to be inhabited
It is not there / it is missing

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the מצוה is done at birth (souls entering bodies). רבי יוחנן: the מצוה needs living children who keep the world inhabited.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
he has not fulfilled the מצוה to have children —
we require "He formed it to be inhabited,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:18

phrases.english: and that is not here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing reasoning, contrasting with רב הונא's reason in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man whose children died has not fulfilled פריה ורביה, since the world is not left inhabited by his children.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces an objection from a ברייתא, aimed at רב הונא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a ברייתא that seems to argue against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיתיבי tells us a source from the תנאים is coming that seems to contradict an אמורא's position. The actual source and the challenge come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רב הונא's position explained in step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a man whose children died has fulfilled פריה ורביה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, quoted next, will be brought to contradict רב הונא.
